Its historical labels and interpretations do not establish present community identity, descent or consent to colonial rule.

appendSections.title: Trade and conditional participation around a mission
appendSections.text: Margaret Swett Henson places El Orcoquisac within competing French and Spanish efforts to control trade in southeastern Texas. Her account distinguishes colonial plans for a mission and presidio from local people’s participation: offers of supplies, disagreements and conditions on settlement shaped their encounters. Read its names, including Orcoquisa and Attakapa, in that eighteenth-century setting. The article is a historian’s reconstruction through earlier documentary scholarship, not a first-person Indigenous account or proof of present affiliations. Its underlying colonial manuscripts still need direct review.

initialAdequacyProposal.rationale: One newly read regional mission-history study adds useful Texas context to the twelve-work guide, bringing the proposed substantive count to thirteen. It does not resolve inconsistent historical names or replace direct colonial-record, archaeological and broader community review. The additional archival dossier located in this pass remains unread and uncounted.

integrationNotes: Preserve the current overview and community distinctions; add only the modest mission-history section and new source. Do not infer equivalence among Orcoquisa/Akokisa, Attakapa, Bidai/Bedais, Deadose or present organized communities from this article.
Keep the direct colonial-archive gap open. This is secondary history, even where it quotes or cites older documents.
Do not adopt the article’s uncorroborated motivational generalizations, dated colonial framing, numerical convert totals, precise archaeological locations or burial-site discussion as Atlas facts.

No new community card or map connection is proposed. Existing original and added access points, first-party accounts, research counts other than the one new work, photographs and rights records remain unchanged.
